thread:
matt-customer: Hey team — trying to finish onboarding for AcmeData but the API key never shows up in the console. CLI returns 401. Can someone help?

sara-support: Sorry for the trouble, matt. Can you paste the exact CLI call + error you see? Also which region / project did you pick during signup?

matt-customer: Sure — we went through the UI (us-east-1) and created the project 'acme-data-prod'. CLI call: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer XXXXXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/current -v
```
Response: 
```json
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "claim_not_active",
  "message": "API credentials not found for project: acme-data-prod"
}
```

sara-support: thanks. That error usually indicates the provisioning claim from the console didn't complete or the service account role wasn't bound. I'll check the provisioning logs. Can you confirm the org id you signed up under (org: acme-ds)?

matt-customer: yes org=acme-ds. We also saw the UI say "Provisioning in progress" for a long time but it never finished.

deploy-bot: [provisioner] claim_created: claim_id=clm_0a1b2c, project=acme-data-prod, status=failed, reason=missing_role_binding

ben-eng: tagging on this. sara — looks like the provisioner failed with missing IAM role on their cloud project. The agent tries to create a service account and bind role `redwood.provisioner` but the customer's project policy prevents new role bindings from being created.

olga-ops: matt, does your org enforce restricted IAM or require an approval workflow for role changes? If so the automated bind would be rejected.

matt-customer: we do have a policy that blocks new editor-like bindings. We didn't realize Redwood needed a service role. What's the minimal permission?

ben-eng: minimal set is a dedicated service role `roles/redwood.provisioner` (create service account, bind role, list service accounts). If you can't allow that, a manual step is possible: have your infra admin create a service account and give it `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` + `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` for the project, then provide us the service account email and we can use it to finish provisioning.

sara-support: matt — two options: 1) grant the `roles/redwood.provisioner` to our provisioning principal (recommended for smoother onboards), or 2) follow ben's manual SA flow. Which can you do?

matt-customer: will ask infra; ETA ~30m. In the meantime, can you share the exact gcloud command I should give to them?

ben-eng: paste this for GCP admins:
```bash
# Grant Redwood provisioner role to service principal (recommended)
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding acme-data-prod \
  --member=serviceAccount:provisioner@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/redwood.provisioner

# OR create a service account and grant narrow perms
gcloud iam service-accounts create redwood-onboard-sa --project=acme-data-prod
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding acme-data-prod \
  --member=serviceAccount:redwood-onboard-sa@acme-data-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountUser
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding acme-data-prod \
  --member=serviceAccount:redwood-onboard-sa@acme-data-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
```

olga-ops: if infra grants the first binding, the provisioner should retry automatically. If they do manual SA, ping me with the SA email and I'll trigger a manual claim reconciliation.

matt-customer: infra gave the green light and ran the first command about 10m ago.

deploy-bot: [provisioner] claim_retry: claim_id=clm_0a1b2c, retry=1

sara-support: I see a retry kicked off. Ben — can you watch the provisioning logs?

ben-eng: watching now... provisioning steps: create SA -> bind roles -> create key -> register key with control plane.

deploy-bot: [provisioner] step=bind_roles status=ok
deploy-bot: [provisioner] step=create_service_account status=ok
deploy-bot: [provisioner] step=create_key status=ok
deploy-bot: [provisioner] step=register_key status=ok

deploy-bot: [provisioner] claim_completed: claim_id=clm_0a1b2c, project=acme-data-prod

olga-ops: I triggered a reconciliation for your project, matt. The key should appear in the console within a few seconds.

matt-customer: I can see the API key now in the console! Making a test call...

matt-customer: curl now returns 200 and key details. Thanks everyone :tada:

sara-support: awesome — glad that fixed it. I'll keep the thread open for one hour in case anything else pops up. If you want, we can document the manual SA steps in your onboarding runbook.

matt-customer: please do, that would help future devs.

tim-oncall: noted — I'll add a short checklist for restricted-iam orgs to the onboarding doc (privs required / manual SA fallback).

sara-support: closing loop: root cause = org-level IAM restrictions blocked automated role binding. Resolution = infra granted `roles/redwood.provisioner` to the provisioning principal, provisioner retried and completed.

matt-customer: thanks again, team.

sara-support: marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
